summary: Extend FEAT-598 linked surfaces so a data-source descriptor can route its fetch through a parrot-server endpoint that executes the query slug and applies a registered Python recipe transformer, giving linked surfaces the same Python aggregation power static/recipe surfaces already have via RecipeRunner.

localization.role: ops XOR ref — the seam where a server-side transformer member is added
descriptor union (kind=query_slug|derived); extension seam for fetch routing
Python lane: fetch + apply_transform; where the recipe transformer runs at bake/refresh
server lane that already hosts both RecipeRunner and LinkedSurfaceService; home of the new per-source data endpoint
the Python transformer contract to reuse: name-registered pure (inputs, params) -> dict with manifests
TS lane fetch URL construction — must branch to the server endpoint when the descriptor declares a Python transformer

constraints.claim: G1 invariant: transformations are referenced by registered name, never stored/executed code — the descriptor must carry a transformer name (+params), resolved against the server's in-process transformer_registry

Python<->TS parity boundary already admits asymmetric transforms: transform.ref is renderer-only (skipped in Python with a warning) and DerivedDataSource forbids ref; the mirror rule applies — a Python transformer is server-only, so the renderer must fetch that source through the server

Server lanes fail closed: LinkedSurfaceService requires a data-plane guard (403 without), owner-check resource is source:read on query_slug:<tenant|public>:<slug>; the new endpoint inherits this trust model
Surface-level server refresh runs with the OWNER's PermissionContext, never the bearer's (spec Known Risk) — the identity model for the new per-source endpoint must be decided explicitly
Snapshot semantics (<=500 rows, mandatory once persisted, GET never executes) and querylimit cap (5000) are unchanged by this feature and must keep holding for transformed sources

hypotheses.statement: Add a third TransformSpec member (e.g. `python: {transformer: <registered name>, params: {...}}`) plus a per-source server data endpoint (e.g. POST /api/v1/ui/surfaces/{surface_id}/sources/{key}/data) on UISurfacesHandler. The endpoint executes the slug via the existing linked executor machinery under the data-plane guard, applies the named transformer from transformer_registry, and returns rows. fetch.ts branches: descriptors with a Python transform fetch from that endpoint instead of QuerySource; the Python executor applies the same transformer at bake/persist/server-refresh time, so Python-lane parity is free (both lanes run the same Python).
hypotheses.reasoning: Every needed primitive exists and converges on UISurfacesHandler: TransformSpec XOR seam, execute_sources, transformer_registry with manifests for fail-fast validation, guard + owner-pctx trust model, and a TS fetch function with a single URL-construction point.

hypotheses.statement: Alternative shape: instead of extending TransformSpec, reuse full recipes — the descriptor references a recipe (name@owner) and the endpoint runs RecipeRunner's transform stage over the slug's frame. Heavier (recipe store dependency, params precedence) but reuses the exact 'recipe definitions' the user names.
hypotheses.reasoning: RecipeRunner is surface-grain (produces whole envelopes), not source-grain; carving out only its transform stage is more invasive than referencing a registered transformer directly. Kept as a design option for /sdd-spec.

confidence_map.claim: FEAT-598 is implemented, documented, and e2e-validated (FEAT-611); this is an enrichment, not greenfield
Linked surfaces today support only inline DSL v1 and renderer-side transform.ref; no Python transformer path exists
The renderer fetches rows directly from QuerySource with the viewer's JWT; no per-source server endpoint exists
The recipe transformer contract ((inputs, params) -> dict, name-registered, manifest-validated) is reusable as-is for linked sources
The server already executes slugs + DSL transforms in Python (LinkedSurfaceService.refresh -> execute_sources), so the new endpoint composes existing machinery
Transformer availability in the server process (which modules get load_transformer_module'd at boot) is operationally solved for recipes and extends to this feature
Client-side DSL ops can still chain after a server-side transformer without breaking dependency ordering

unknowns.question: Identity model for the new per-source data endpoint: run the slug under the VIEWER's JWT/PBAC (like today's direct QuerySource fetch) or under the surface OWNER's PermissionContext (like the surface-level server refresh)?
options: Viewer identity — preserves today's per-viewer data scoping; transformer runs on what the viewer may see
Owner identity — matches the server-refresh lane; simpler, but shows owner-scoped data to any viewer with surface access
Viewer identity with owner fallback only for share-token viewers (hybrid)
unknowns.user_answer: Viewer identity (JWT): the endpoint executes the slug under the viewer's QuerySource PBAC, preserving today's per-viewer data scoping. For share-token viewers (see U4) there is no JWT, so those requests run under the OWNER's PermissionContext, mirroring the existing share server-refresh semantics (spec Known Risk).

unknowns.question: What does the descriptor reference: a bare registered transformer name (transformer_registry, G1-style) or a recipe (name@owner from the recipe store) whose transform steps run over the slug frame?
options: Both, transformer name first, recipe ref as a later increment
unknowns.user_answer: Both, phased: v1 references a registered transformer by name (+params) against transformer_registry (G1 intact); a recipe reference (name@owner via the recipe store) is a planned later increment, not in v1 scope.

unknowns.question: May a server-transformed source still carry inline DSL ops (applied after the transformer) and be referenced by derived siblings / join-union ops, or is the Python transformer terminal for that source in v1?
options: Terminal in v1 — transformer output is the frame, no chaining (simplest)
Allow DSL ops after the transformer in both lanes
Allow derived siblings to reference it but no same-source chaining
unknowns.user_answer: Terminal in v1: the transformer's output IS the source's frame. No inline DSL ops after it and no derived/join/union sibling may reference a python-transformed source in v1.

unknowns.question: Is the new endpoint available to share-token viewers (server executes on their behalf, like the share refresh button), or authenticated sessions only in v1?
options: Authenticated only in v1; share viewers keep snapshot-only
Share viewers included from day one (matches existing share refresh semantics)
unknowns.user_answer: Share-token viewers are included from day one: the server executes slug+transformer on their behalf under the owner's pctx (consistent with the existing share refresh), returning the transformed rows.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence, all primitives exist and converge on known seams; the open questions are design decisions (identity, reference grain, chaining), which the spec's Open Questions / intake can carry after the Q&A below.
